html:
Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden. On the map it covers the late years of French Somaliland and the republic that followed in 1977.

Its people are mainly Afar and Somali Issa. In the Middle Ages the coast fell within the sultanates of Ifat and Adal. France bought the port of Obock in 1862 and built the town of Djibouti from 1888. A railway to Addis Ababa, finished in 1917, made it the main sea outlet of the Ethiopian Empire.

  • 1967: renamed the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas.
  • 1977: independence.
  • 1991 to 2000: a civil war between the government and Afar rebels, ended by a power-sharing deal.

Its position beside one of the world's busiest shipping lanes brings in foreign bases. France, the United States and, since 2017, China all keep troops there.
sum: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden. On the map it covers the late years of French Somaliland and the republic that followed in 1977.
